newsitem.title: CANADA: Royal Bank off after broker downgrades stock.
newsitem.headline: Royal Bank off after broker downgrades stock.

text.p: Shares in Royal Bank of Canada fell on the Toronto Stock Exchange on Monday after an influential U.S. investment firm cut its rating on Canada's largest bank.
Royal Bank's stock was off 0.70 at 49.15 in late morning turnover of 797,000 shares.
New York-based Morgan Stanley & Co Inc earlier downgraded the bank's stock to neutral from outperform.
Morgan Stanley analyst Nigel Dally said Royal Bank -- which has rallied along with other Canadian bank shares this autumn -- is now fairly valued.
"The downgrade is purely on price. We continue to like the stock, but we think it has moved up to a price where it is now fairly valued," Dally said in a telephone interview.
Fuelled by low interest rates and strong interest from foreign investors, Canadian bank stocks have enjoyed a sustained rally since early September.

The TSE's banks and trusts index has added over 1600 points in the past three months -- powering the overall market to record highs. "If the TSE goes up we believe Royal will continue to go up with it, but we don't see a lot of outperformance for the stock," Dally said.
Morgan Stanley also has neutral ratings on Canadian Imperial Bank of Commerce, Bank of Montreal, and Bank of Nova Scotia.
Toronto-Dominion Bank continues to hold an outperform rating.
"As a group I think they are reaching the upper limits of what I would consider fair value," Dally said.
Among other active bank stocks, TD-Bank was off 1.10 at 34.90, CIBC fell 0.60 to 60.10, Bank of Montreal dropped 0.60 to 43.20, and Scotiabank surrendered 0.60 to 46.10.
